title: Mexico City Point Clouds
excerpt: Scanning Mexico City myself, and finding out what the buildings become once they are only measurement and light.
description:
Ongoing research in Mexico City, built from my own LiDAR scans rather than from open aerial data. I walk the buildings and scan them at close range, so the cloud carries the position I stood in, what the scanner could see from there and what it could not.
Landmarks such as the Palacio de Bellas Artes come back as millions of points, dense where I stayed and thin where I passed.
> This one is research, not an edition series. Scanning a city yourself is slower and more partial than taking the data from the air, and that partiality is the point: what you get is not the building, it is the record of an encounter with it.
credits: Own LiDAR scans, point cloud work and rendering: Jaco Schilp. Mexico City.
